title: A joined thread's own children: derive their joins before it ends
why: W47-CONDVAR-JOIN-PUBLICATION's C5 rule (gateway rule 10q) discharges a release only after a checked join of every live retaining thread, and a joined thread's children are not joined by it (POSIX: a thread's termination does not end the threads it started). On the in_tail test binary at 90978ac6 the engine thread flb_lib_worker starts retaining threads the census derives (the input worker input_thread among them; 4 retaining descendants at the fixed test's releases, 9 counting every live thread at flb_destroy), and the engine's own join of the input worker is unchecked (src/flb_input_thread.c:607, `pthread_join(tid, NULL); ... return 0;`, B51). Every release under the fixed non-threaded test therefore carries this unresolved reason in addition to R2. DISCHARGE: a derivation, over the engine thread's own paths to its end, of a checked join of each retaining child (or a premise with its reading pinned), measured on the census.

title: Feed the condvar/join census into the audit routes
why: The per-unit resource routes (quirin-audit pinned/current) derive no thread, predicate loop or join, so they refuse every call to a declared thread-synchronization callee (rule 10q, contract spec C04.10): 6 corpus call sites (Monkey mk_clock_exit, mk_stop, mk_sched_launch_worker_loop, mk_sched_launch_thread, mk_sched_init, mk_sched_workers_join), 0 system and the slice sites listed in the report now carry `outside its declared thread-synchronization obligation`, every one in an Unknown function. The census route (quirin_source_analysis::condvar_join_census) is a separate read of one program. DISCHARGE: a whole-program census phase whose per-site answers reach the per-unit routes, with its inputs in the run identity; measured on the three routes (with W47-LOOP-OWNER-AUDIT-ROUTE).

title: Condvar census reading gaps outside the in_tail track
why: Over the 1,685 files of the in_tail test binary at 90978ac6 the census decides the bound sites and refuses or leaves unresolved the rest. Not discharged by reading gaps, not findings: the pre-spawn initialisation of a caller-supplied object is not a derived quiescent phase (src/flb_log.c:1156 `log->pth_init = FLB_FALSE` before flb_worker_create; lib/monkey/mk_server/mk_scheduler.c:431 `server->pth_init`), a base whose struct type the reader does not key makes a held mutex unknown (src/flb_chunk_trace.c:176), and a wait loop whose body is more than a wait, or whose mutex the enclosing loop's join loses, is not read (src/flb_downstream_worker.c:256, :593). Unresolved: 11 destroy, 9 init, 15 read, 6 wait, 3 signal and 1 broadcast sites (fixed revision), mostly field keys through nested bases and bodies the statement reader refuses (`goto`, `switch`, a conditional group splitting a statement: 251 of the 1,177 bodies it reads). A lone wait outside a predicate loop (src/flb_chunk_trace.c:312) is a kept refusal, not a defect claim. DISCHARGE: a pre-spawn phase for caller-supplied objects, nested-base keys, and a CFG reading of `goto`/`switch`, each measured on the census.

title: Derive the condvar census's stated premises
why: Rule 10q states, and does not prove: P-SYNC-INSTANCE (a field-keyed condvar, mutex or guarded field names one object per instance, and a waiter and its signaller name the same one: the worker handshake's thi->init_condition is per input instance); P-JOIN-IDENTITY (a thread identifier stored in a field is the one the same context spawned: flb_stop's ctx->config->worker is do_start's tid); P-RETAIN (the test's published storage and the fixture are retained only by threads that run the tail input's or the test's code, taken from the loop-owner census's contexts, whose field-keyed V over-approximates); P-CHECK (acutest's TEST_CHECK is its argument's truth, read from tests/lib/acutest/acutest.h:85 and :662-722). DISCHARGE: a data-flow derivation of the instance, the thread identifier and the retained storage (points-to over the published address), or narrower premises with their readings pinned.
